target_customer: DNA synthesis providers, biotech firms and AI x bio model developers needing biosecurity screening
problem: AI makes biology easier to engineer, raising misuse risk; defenders lack tooling for customer screening, functional sequence screening and model safeguards.
business_model: B2B biosecurity infrastructure (customer screening module live; pricing not public)

founders.name: Evan Seeyave
founders.background_notes: Automated testing at Google and AI evaluations at SecureBio per the YC page; EBRC lists him as a council member.

founders.name: Harmon Bhasin
founders.background_notes: Named as a TwentyTwo founder in the LatchBio acquisition post.

founders.name: John Wang
founders.background_notes: Named as a TwentyTwo founder in the LatchBio acquisition post.

competitors.name: Aclid
competitors.what: Commercial customer and sequence screening for DNA synthesis providers
competitors.traction_then: used by synthesis companies per a Manifund page
competitors.funding_then: $3.3M seed (SynBioBeta headline; date not verified here)

competitors.name: SecureDNA
competitors.what: Free nonprofit sequence screening using cryptographic matching
competitors.traction_then: free software offered to synthesis providers

competitors.name: Battelle UltraSEQ
competitors.traction_then: in NIST blinded test alongside Aclid, IBBIS, RTX BBN

competitors.name: safely.bio
competitors.what: Know-your-customer checks for DNA synthesis orders

technical_complexity.rationale: Agent-based background research for customer screening is standard engineering; functional screening of sequences that evade BLAST is research-grade but was listed as coming soon.

defensibility.rationale: Possible compliance and trust position if screening becomes mandated, but at founding several screening vendors and a free nonprofit tool existed and no lock-in is shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; the team was acquired by LatchBio, announced 2026-06-29.

market_need_then: A May 2025 US executive order called for verifiable nucleic acid screening (per a secondary source, not checked against the order); sources note customer screening standards are less mature than sequence screening.

identity.logo: Logo image exists but is not described in sources
identity.visual_style: Large statistics and bold headlines per site fetch
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct: "Papers you can cite. Systems you can run."

rebrands.why: Acquired by LatchBio; team leads Latch Biosecurity

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand; an unrelated Dutch firm (TwentyTwo Security) shares the name; the brand was folded into Latch within about a year.

outcome_analysis: TwentyTwo, a three-person Summer 2025 biosecurity team, was acquired by LatchBio on 2026-06-29, about a year after the batch, with undisclosed terms. No funding round was found, so it is unclear whether this was a soft landing or a strategic exit. The founders' SecureBio evaluation background and a policy tailwind on screening fit the story, but the sources do not give traction or customers.
